verdict:
FLAT, PRINT-GATED - the brief's arithmetic was evidentially contaminated, red proved it, and the same bear conclusion re-derives from clean vetted numbers anyway.

WHAT I RE-VERIFIED MYSELF. Blue's reconstruction is the load-bearing structure of this verdict, so I proxy-fetched the vetted Q2 8-K ex99 myself. It states verbatim: 'Net income is expected to be between $71.0 million and $101.0 million' with adjusted EBITDA '$275 million to $325 million' maintained, and 'targeted gross margins by segment are 10% to 12% for the Utilities and 6% to 8% in Energy segments for the full year 2026.' The same release prints Q2 net loss $24.2M (vs +$84.3M LY), Energy gross LOSS -0.3% vs +10.8%, Utilities 11.9% vs 14.1%, H1 adjusted EBITDA $71.9M. Blue is exact on every figure. The vetted arithmetic therefore stands on its own: H2 must deliver $77.7-107.7M of net income after a losing H1, H2 adjusted EBITDA must run 2.8-3.5x H1, and at flat H2 revenue the Energy segment must print ~8.4-12.4% gross margin in the same year management says 'historical 10-12%' returns only in 2027. The maintained guide is internally strained in exactly the direction the brief claimed - on numbers the brief never used.

WHAT DIED AND MUST STAY DEAD. The brief's headline constructs were contaminated: the Q3/Q4 EBITDA stack and the $150-200M FCF guide exist in NO vetted document (transcript/secondary only - and the brief's '6-8% in Q3, 8-10% in Q4' misread FY segment targets as a quarterly path); AR is $839.1M not $1,715M (the scary unbilled contract-asset line is FLAT at $937.7M); net debt is $582.9M from net CASH $62.8M, not $415M-to-$1,061M; the 1.6x leverage 'anomaly' was manufactured by the brief's own wrong net debt (actual ~1.94x on guide midpoint, covenant-compliant, though red's 'reconciles fine' stays PLAUSIBLE until someone pulls the credit agreement definition - neither bench did). Court-worthiness was scored on precisely the claims that failed venue-diff; blue's restoration to ~6/10 on the vetted legs is right.

THE SWING FACTOR BOTH BENCHES AGREE ON: $244.0M of unapproved contract modifications, $205.9M ALREADY RECOGNIZED as revenue, retainage $291.3M and already declining ($311.2M->$291.3M) - retainage release is running and still could not stop -$131.3M of H1 OCF. Change-order approval is the cash mechanism that rescues H2; failure is further reversals on top of the -$87.6M of H1 estimate changes. That line is the print's real headline, whatever the EPS says.

DAMAGE CLASS: DAMAGE-ARRIVING stands on all three records - Energy printed a gross LOSS, and 4 of the 6 problem projects were still open at 6/30 (3 due substantially complete in Q3, 1 by year-end). The $13.9B record backlog and $3.9B of new awards keep this from being STRUCTURAL - the franchise is intact; the question is whether the 2026 bridge holds.

GATE RULING: the existing ledger gate (alert_below 65.0, 52-week-low breach, full re-court) is KEPT as informational - PRIM has no exogenous commodity carrier (utility/energy construction demand is the cycle, and the stress is idiosyncratic execution), and the path finding (blue's corrected read: dip to ~$75, +11% recovery, NOT red's V-to-$65 which conflated the 52-week low with the June cut) says the market is re-rating INTO the maintained guide. A print miss from $83 has room to fall through $65; the gate would then correctly force a re-court rather than an entry.
blue_ruling: PARTIALLY OVERTURNED in the most instructive way this batch: red's factual demolition of the brief was almost entirely SUSTAINED (five refutations on primaries - the transcript-only quarterly stack, the phantom FCF guide, the $1,715M AR aggregation artifact, the $1,061M net-debt error, the manufactured leverage anomaly), but red's bottom line ('one leg survives') was OVERTURNED because red stopped at demolition: blue rebuilt the identical hockey-stick from FULLY VETTED documents - FY net income guide $71-101M against a filed H1 net LOSS of -$6.7M, and an FY Energy gross-margin target of 6-8% against H1 actual 3.6%. I re-fetched the Q2 ex99 per doctrine and blue's reconstruction is verbatim in the release, digit for digit.
reopen_gates: DATA (primary, print ~2026-11-02): Q3 Energy gross margin vs the implied ~8.4-12.4% H2 requirement, Q3 OCF vs the -$131.3M H1 hole, and the unapproved-change-order balance vs $244.0M/$205.9M recognized. Guide held AND Energy GM inside the requirement AND change orders converting to cash = the bridge is real; re-court for a starter on the intact-franchise story ($13.9B backlog).

EVENT: any pre-announcement 8-K (guide revision, project charge, change-order settlement) - the twice-cut guide's third cut, if coming, likely arrives before the print; treat any intraquarter 8-K as a pack-early-resolution trigger.

DATA: change-order approval or reversal disclosure in any venue - the $205.9M recognized-but-unapproved balance is the single number that converts the FCF story from hope to arithmetic in either direction.
EVENT: a company PR fixing the Q3 print date (Q2's was PR'd ~2 weeks ahead) - re-key the pack and run the T-minus-5 reconstruction on the vetted legs.

DATA (before any leverage claim is ever load-bearing): the credit agreement's leverage definition - red's '1.6x reconciles with addbacks' remains PLAUSIBLE-only; both benches flagged it, neither pulled it.

PRICE (existing ledger gate, kept): alert_below 65.0 = 52-week-low breach -> new-low regime, full re-court, never entry (the fill would arrive via a print miss or a third cut - thesis-worse by construction).
